newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-BOLIVIA STRUGGLE TO NARROW WIN OVER VENEZUELA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BOLIVIA STRUGGLE TO NARROW WIN OVER VENEZUELA.

text.p: Host nation Bolivia struggled to a 1-0 win over Venezuela, the weakest team in the tournament, in their opening Copa America game on Thursday.
Venezuela had conceeded a total of 13 goals in their previous two visits to La Paz, which lies 3,600 meters above sea level, but defended stubbornly to keep the Bolivia to a single goal.
Midfielder Milton Coimbra saved Bolivian blushes when he scored with a clever backheel to flick home a cross by Luis Cristaldo in the 60th minute.
Venezuela goalkeeper Rafael Dudamel made four world class saves from long range shots in the closing minutes to keep the score down but Venezuela rarely looked like suffering another humiliation.
The underdogs seemed unaffected by the thin air, even though they had arrived only two days earlier. The two teams had met in Venezuela in a World Cup qualifier on Sunday in a game which ended 1-1.

Only 10,000 fans watched Bolivia's debut. The poor attendance was blamed on recent poor performances by the team in the World Cup qualifiers and a general feeling they had distanced themselves from the public by imposing a media silence on Tuesday.

Bolivia defender Juan Manuel Pena was sent off in the second half, apparently for dissent after he had earlier been booked. Venezuela's David MacIntosh was later dismissed for a wild challenge on an opponent.
